help.html:
How SiteSizer sizes a location

Every input change instantly recalculates the BoM, diagram, IP plan and power. All numbers below come from the catalog — you can change them in “Catalog”.

1. Growth reserve

When enabled, sockets, cameras and access points (each zone separately) are multiplied by (1 + {reserve}%) and rounded up before switches are sized — so the reserve may add a switch.

2. Switches

    {cats}

Base or premium model. Premium models have two hot-swap power supplies. They are recommended for important sites (tiers 1–2), and the app asks you to confirm. If the APs need more 802.3bt PoE ports (FAP-241K, FAP-441K) than FS-124G-FPOE offers (8), FS-624F-FPOE (24 × 802.3bt) is selected automatically.

PoE. AP draw comes from datasheets, camera draw from the “Camera power draw” field (default {cam} W). A warning appears above {warn}% of the budget; if the budget is short, switches are added.

3. Core (aggregation)

“Auto” adds the FS-1024E only with more than {core_sw} switches and more than {core_floors} floors (thresholds live in Catalog → Rules). “Yes” — always, “No” — never. A core needs a FortiGate with 10G SFP+, so FG-80F is skipped. When one FS-1024E can't take all switches, another core group is added.

4. FortiGate

The first model in the ladder that passes every limit is chosen: FortiSwitch count, FortiAP count, 10G ports (with a core) and, if inspected traffic is given, threat-protection throughput with {head}% headroom.

{ladder}

5. Criticality tiers

{tiers}
TierAddsSLA

6. Racks, DACs, power

Cabinets follow the house standard: ODF on top, then FortiGate and core, then organizer · patch panels · organizer · switch · organizer … — every switch sits between organizers, a 48-port switch has one panel above and one below. PDUs and UPS at the bottom. Names: CODE-FloorLetter-ASW01 (access), WSW (Wi-Fi), VSW (video), CSW (core), FW. On the Racks page you drag devices and add or remove cabinets.

DACs follow the layout: devices in one cabinet closer than {dac_u}U get a 1 m DAC; bottom ↔ top or different cabinets get a 3 m DAC. Remote closets (run > 90 m) use fibre and transceivers.

Power comes from datasheets plus the real PoE load with PSU efficiency; the UPS has {ups}% headroom. Uplink oversubscription should stay below {oversub}:1.

7. IP plan

Enter the location ID (second octet) and every VLAN gets a subnet from the template {template} with a gateway (first address) and a DHCP pool. Double-click a VLAN ID, name or mask to change it; you can add your own VLANs. When a /24 can't hold the devices plus {buf}% headroom you get a warning — use a larger mask. Without an ID, subnets are carved from the base network.

8. Checks

The checks panel shows three levels: error (will not work), warning (worth reviewing), note (good to know). Some have action buttons — e.g. confirming dual power supplies.

Keyboard

Tab next field, arrows ±1, Ctrl+K command palette, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+E export (Excel, PDF, pictures) / Ctrl+P PDF.
